AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Controlling Soil Pollution? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Controlling Soil Pollution.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Controlling Soil Pollution.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Controlling Soil Pollution.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Controlling Soil Pollution.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Trees? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Trees.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Trees.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Trees.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Trees.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Selected Crop Management Practises? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Selected Crop Management Practises.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Selected Crop Management Practises.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Selected Crop Management Practises.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Selected Crop Management Practises.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Food Nutrients.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Food Nutrients.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Food Nutrients.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Food Nutrients.

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Establishment Planting Site? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Establishment Planting Site.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Constructing Water Retention Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Constructing Water Retention Structures.

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

17. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

18. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

19. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. joule (J)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food.

21. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking Food and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Hygiene in Rearing Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Knitting Skills 10 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Laundry: Loose- coloured Items and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Knitting Skills 10 4.2 Constructing Framed Suspended Garden 10 4.3 Adding Value  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Knitting Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

31. In three clear sentences, explain Constructing Framed Suspended Garden and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

32. In three clear sentences, explain Adding Value to Crop Produce 8 4.4 Making Homemade Soap 8 Total Number of Lesson and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
